headline: Approved up to $90,000 to buy bleachers for Memorial Field, plus a committee to study district revenue.
summary: The meeting covered Memorial Field bleachers, enrollment and class sizes, a federal scholarship tax credit, and the Rundlett Middle School name. Members approved up to $90,000 for bleachers and waived the bidding policy for that purchase. They also created a revenue committee and voted to offer the City first refusal on properties for sale.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda as amended, 9-0.
Created an ad hoc committee to study ways to increase district revenue, 9-0.
Directed administration to notify the City of Concord and offer its right of first refusal on properties for sale, 9-0.
Requested that a Board representative and staff be included in talks on a possible Steeplegate mall TIF district, 9-0.
Waived Policy 322 for the bleacher purchase, passed unanimously by voice vote.
Authorized up to $90,000 for bleachers for Memorial Field, 9-0 by roll call.

Board of Education Minutes – September 1, 2026 
 
Board members present: Pamela Walsh – President, Cara Meeker – Vice President, Liz Boucher – 
Secretary, Jess Campbell, Alex Dubois, Brenda Hastings, Barb Higgins, Madeleine Mineau, and Sarah 
Sadowski 
 
Board members absent: none 
 
Administrators/Staff: Timothy Herbert – Superintendent, Matt Cashman, Jack Dunn, Bridget Edinger, 
Kris Gallo, Michele Garon, Kaily Roukey 
 
Call to Order 
Ms. Walsh called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM and asked Ms. Boucher to take roll call attendance. 
 
Approval of Agenda 
The Board noted that the Memorial Field item would remain on the agenda for informational 
purposes, as the anticipated joint City/School District meeting had not yet occurred. 
 
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to approve the Agenda (Moved by Ms. Meeker, 2nd by Ms. 
Campbell). 
 
Consent Agenda 
a. City & Community Relations (July 17) 
b. Regular Monthly Meeting (August 3) 
c. Finance Committee (August 12) 
d. Instructional Committee (August 12) 
e. Executive Committee (August 17) 
f. City & Community Relations (August 17) 
g. Communication & Policy (August 19) 
Ms. Higgins requested removal of the City and Community Relations minutes from the Consent 
Agenda because the published minutes were from an incorrect meeting and would be republished in 
a future board packet. 
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to remove the minutes of the City and Community Relations 
meeting from the consent Agenda (Moved by Ms. Higgins, 2nd by Ms. Mineau) 
The following corrections were identified:
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – September 1, 2026 
 
• Page 15: Note that Ms. Higgins submitted the amendments to the July 15 City and Community 
Relations minutes. 
• Page 18: Correct the spelling of Josh Hardy's name. 
• Page 22: Correct the Finance Committee’s minutes to reflect that the August 12 meeting was 
called to order at 5:00 p.m. 
The Board voted 9-0, via vice vote, to approve the Consent Agenda as amended (Moved by Ms. 
Boucher, 2nd by Ms. Higgins). 
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to approve the revised Consent Agenda (Moved by Ms. Hastings 
2nd by Ms. Meeker). 
 
Recognitions & Reports 
Student Representative Clementine Mayala welcomed everyone back for the new school year and 
shared her excitement about continuing to serve on the Board. She noted that she will be working 
with Mr. Corkum to help identify candidates for the current student representative vacancy.  
 
Clementine highlighted several upcoming student activities, including Picture Days, the Club Fair on 
September 18, the Multicultural Festival on September 20, and Homecoming Weekend later in the 
month, which students are eagerly anticipating. She also brought forward student concerns regarding 
Memorial Field, noting that with football season underway, there has been considerable discussion 
and uncertainty about how issues related to the field may affect homecoming events and activities. 
 
Superintendent Herbert welcomed staff and students back for the new school year and reported a 
successful opening across the district. Staff participated in a districtwide welcome-back event at 
Concord High School, where two awards were presented. Laurel Gorvitz, a sixth-grade student at 
Rundlett Middle School, received the Sergeant Memorial Award for a patriotic essay written as a fifth-
grade student at Christa McAuliffe School. Susan Farrelly received the Bob Silva Award in recognition 
of her exceptional service to students and families through her leadership of after-school programs, 
transportation services, family support initiatives, and summer meal partnerships. 
 
Superintendent Herbert introduced Transportation Director, Rebecka Hart, who reported a 
significantly smoother start to the school year, with most Rundlett Middle School buses arriving by 
approximately 8:30 a.m., reflecting notable improvements over previous years. She credited the 
transportation team and bus company for their efforts while acknowledging that some typical start-
of-year adjustments are still being made. She also addressed a ParentSquare spreadsheet error that 
resulted in some families receiving incorrect bus route information. The issue was identified and 
corrected by ParentSquare before the start of school, and transportation staff worked quickly to 
provide accurate routing information to affected families. 
Over the summer, the transportation department conducted a comprehensive review of bus routes 
to improve efficiency and service. The review focused on balancing ridership across buses, reducing 
overcrowding, maximizing available seating, improving arrival times, and keeping student ride times 
under 45 minutes whenever possible. Ms. Hart also discussed requests from families in designated 
walk zones who are seeking bus transportation. These requests are being reviewed on an ongoing 
basis, and while October has been communicated as a possible timeline, it represents a worst-case
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – September 1, 2026 
 
scenario rather than an expected completion date. Requests are being considered as route capacities 
are finalized to avoid creating overcrowded buses later in the year. 
Challenges in route planning continue to arise from student address changes and delays in updating 
PowerSchool records during the summer months. Board members discussed opportunities to 
improve the process, including sending annual student information updates earlier in the summer, 
enhancing communication with families about address changes, and streamlining portions of the 
annual update process. Ms. Hart also reported that the district continues to experience a bus driver 
shortage. To maintain transportation services, office staff may occasionally assist by driving routes, 
and route consolidations may be necessary when staffing levels are limited. Despite these ongoing 
challenges, the transportation department has made significant improvements in service delivery and 
remains focused on strengthening staffing, communication, and route efficiency throughout the 
school year. 
Superintendent Herbert introduced the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) program, a new federal 
initiative expected to take effect on January 1, 2027. The program would allow individuals and 
organizations to direct up to $1,700 of their federal tax liability to approved Scholarship Granting 
Organizations (SGOs), which would then provide scholarships to eligible students. These scholarships 
could be used to support a variety of educational expenses, including transportation for internships 
and career-connected learning opportunities, co-curricular participation fees, educational equipment, 
supplies, and other approved student-related costs. 
Administration explained that scholarship funds are expected to be awarded directly to individual 
students rather than to school districts, and that additional guidance from federal and state agencies 
is still forthcoming. The district has begun discussions with the New Hampshire Secretary of State's 
Office, the Attorney General's Office, and potential Scholarship Granting Organizations to better 
understand how the program could be implemented and how it may benefit Concord students. Board 
members discussed potential uses of the scholarships, eligibility requirements, similarities and 
differences between the program and New Hampshire's Education Freedom Account (EFA) program, 
and how the initiative might support existing district opportunities. Members noted the need for 
additional information and background materials before determining how the district may engage 
with the program.  
Superintendent Herbert presented the results of the district's school naming feedback process 
conducted under Board Policy 735. The district gathered input through ParentSquare, the district 
website, social media, local media outreach, and direct submissions, receiving 722 responses, 
including 211 from students.  
 
The most frequently suggested names were Rundlett Middle School (195 submissions) and Concord 
Middle School (115 submissions). Supporters of retaining the Rundlett name emphasized preserving 
local history, honoring Louis Rundlett's contributions, maintaining alumni connections and the Blue 
Dukes identity, and avoiding costs associated with changing uniforms, signage, athletic equipment, 
and other materials. Additional suggestions included names honoring local figures and historically 
significant community and Indigenous names.
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – September 1, 2026 
 
Based on the survey results and community feedback, Superintendent Herbert recommended 
retaining the name Rundlett Middle School, citing strong public support, the school's historical 
significance, preservation of traditions and identity, and cost savings. 
 
During Board discussion, members reviewed next steps in the decision-making process, public access 
to submission data, possible public hearing requirements, and whether consideration of the school 
mascot should be separated from the naming decision. Board members also discussed arguments for 
Concord Middle School, including alignment with Concord High School, greater recognition outside 
the district, and a stronger connection to the broader community. Questions were raised about 
potential confusion with Christa McAuliffe School (CMS), the meaning of "broader community 
inclusion" cited in some submissions, and the public release of the full submission summary. 
Administration stated that the complete summary would be made public following Board review.  
 
Preschool Scholarship Rubric Update 
Director of Student Services Kailey Roukey presented proposed revisions to the district's preschool 
tuition scholarship procedures following the adoption of updated preschool tuition rates. The 
revisions include new family notification materials, scholarship forms, and a scholarship rubric 
intended to provide clearer guidance on eligibility requirements and program expectations. Ms. 
Roukey noted that federal regulations require preschool scholarship applications to remain separate 
from free and reduced-price meal applications, although scholarship eligibility continues to be based 
on federal income guidelines. 
 
The updated procedures establish attendance and participation expectations for families receiving 
tuition assistance due to limited enrollment capacity and waitlists. New provisions also address 
outstanding tuition balances and program participation requirements. The revised scholarship model 
introduces both full tuition scholarships and 50 percent partial scholarships, replacing the previous 
all-or-nothing approach and allowing the district to support more families with available funding. 
Scholarship awards are currently limited to two opportunities per preschool site, generally 
designated for one three-year-old and one four-year-old student, with partial scholarships available 
based on demonstrated need and available resources. 
 
Board members discussed the history of preschool tuition assistance, the possibility of families 
qualifying for New Hampshire childcare scholarship programs, and whether future Federal 
Scholarship Tax Credit opportunities could provide additional support. Administration agreed to 
investigate available state and federal funding sources that may help expand access to preschool 
programs.  
 
National Study of Special Education Spending 
Kailey Roukey, Director of Student Services, presented information regarding a national study 
examining special education expenditures, which is the first major national review of special 
education spending in approximately twenty years. Concord was selected as one of ten New 
Hampshire school districts to participate, and the New Hampshire Department of Education has 
encouraged districts to take part while confirming the legitimacy of the study. Ms. Roukey explained 
that the district has received only limited information about the study's requirements and data 
collection process thus far, although researchers have indicated that student information and district 
data submitted for the study will remain confidential.
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – September 1, 2026 
 
 
Board members expressed several concerns and emphasized the need for caution before 
participating. Discussion focused on whether data provided to researchers would be anonymized, the 
lack of detailed guidance accompanying the request, safeguards for data privacy and confidentiality, 
whether the study has received the appropriate university or institutional review approvals, the 
amount of staff time that participation may require, and the proposed use of gift cards or stipends as 
compensation for participants. Administration indicated that no district information would be 
submitted until additional details are available and The Board's questions have been fully addressed. 
Board members stressed the importance of protecting student privacy and ensuring that all 
appropriate safeguards are in place before moving forward.  
 
Rundlett Middle School Groundbreaking Ceremony 
Administration provided an update on plans for a groundbreaking ceremony celebrating the start of 
construction on the new Rundlett Middle School. Principal Jay Richard reported that initial planning 
discussions have begun and that a tentative ceremony is being considered for September 26 at 
approximately 9:00 a.m. The event is expected to last about 30 minutes and would be coordinated 
with Homecoming activities later that day to encourage broad community participation. 
 
Board members expressed support for holding the ceremony during Homecoming weekend to 
maximize attendance and community engagement. Discussion centered on coordinating the 
ceremony with the Homecoming parade schedule, inviting community members and project partners, 
and managing logistical details such as ceremonial groundbreaking shovels. 
 
Mr. Richard stated that he will continue working with district administration to organize the event, 
coordinate invitations, and finalize plans. Administration noted that additional details and the 
finalized schedule will be shared in future Board communications.  
 
Rundlett Middle School Construction Impact 
Board members discussed the impact of construction of the new Rundlett Middle School on students 
and staff, particularly regarding construction noise. Principal Jay Richard reported that while 
construction activity is more noticeable outdoors, noise inside the school has not significantly 
disrupted learning or daily operations, and students and staff have adapted well. School activities, 
including athletics, recess, and emergency procedures, continue as normal, while grade-level 
assemblies are being held to keep students informed and address questions about the project.  
 
Administration will continue coordinating with construction personnel to minimize impacts during 
important academic activities, such as state assessments and testing periods. Mr. Richard noted that 
the current site work phase is expected to be the loudest portion of the project, with noise levels 
anticipated to decrease as construction progresses. Board members encouraged ongoing monitoring 
of conditions and discussed potential accommodations, such as earplugs, should noise become 
disruptive.  
Capital Facilities 
Mr. Cashman highlighted several summer facilities improvements, including additional classroom 
space and welding stations at Concord High School, sidewalk repairs at Beaver Meadow and Christa 
McAuliffe schools, painting projects, and districtwide deep cleaning. Mr. Cashman took a moment to
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – September 1, 2026 
 
recognize the Facilities Department, maintenance team, custodians, and support personnel for their 
efforts preparing schools for the new year. 
 
Mr. Cashman also reported that construction of the new Rundlett Middle School is progressing well 
and remains slightly ahead of schedule. Foundation work, geothermal well installation, and site 
infrastructure improvements are underway, with approximately 75 percent of underground 
infrastructure completed. Noise and vibration levels continue to be monitored, with no significant 
concerns reported. A project budget update, including the Guaranteed Maximum Price, is expected in 
October. The Board discussed a humidity-related issue at Beaver Meadow School that affected eight 
classrooms. After remediation and independent testing, the area was cleared for occupancy, and 
administration continues to monitor the performance of the HVAC system. 
 
Finance 
The Finance Committee reviewed the district's early-year financial status, noting that budget reports 
currently do not reflect the full impact of payroll and contractual commitments for school-year 
employees. Administration reported that state adequacy aid was approximately $720,000 lower than 
anticipated, creating a budget challenge, though higher-than-expected special education aid may help 
offset some of the shortfall. A year-end FY26 financial review and possible FY27 budget adjustments 
will be presented at future meetings. 
 
The committee also discussed three recommendations for Board consideration: establishing a 
committee to explore new revenue-generating opportunities through facility use and community 
programming; sending a letter to the City of Concord regarding potential interest in district properties 
that may be considered for sale; and requesting district participation in discussions related to any 
potential Tax Increment Financing (TIF) district associated with the redevelopment of the Steeplegate 
Mall property due to possible impacts on future school revenues and enrollment. 
 
Communications & Policy 
Ms. Meeker presented a new Open Enrollment Policy for first reading. The policy was developed 
collaboratively by the Policy Committee and district administration in anticipation of new open 
enrollment requirements.  
 
The Board reviewed the proposed Open Enrollment Policy, which would allow up to 30 full-time 
students, equivalent to 180 course seats, while setting outgoing open enrollment at zero. 
Administration explained that the outgoing limit helps minimize district liability while preserving 
existing procedures for families to request transfers through the Superintendent and School Board. 
Board members discussed the distinction between the 30-student limit and 180-seat capacity, noting 
that the enrollment cap is based on current staffing levels and can be accommodated without 
additional staff. The Board was informed that a public hearing is required before action can be taken 
on the policy and agreed to discuss scheduling the hearing during the calendar review. 
 
 
City & Community Relations 
The Board received an update on Memorial Field and the ongoing impact of the condemned and 
removed bleachers. Administration emphasized that the discussion was informational only and that 
no funding currently exists in the budget for the options presented. Athletic Director Steve Largy
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – September 1, 2026 
 
reported that current conditions at Memorial Field necessitate relocating the first home football game 
to the National Guard Field, creating transportation and event management challenges and limiting 
the traditional game-day experience. Despite these challenges, administration expressed optimism 
that the remaining home games, including Homecoming, could be hosted at Memorial Field. 
 
Administration outlined options for addressing the lack of seating, including renting temporary 
bleachers for the remainder of the football season, or purchasing mobile bleachers that could be used 
at Memorial Field for several years and potentially relocated to future athletic facilities. Rental costs 
were estimated at approximately $22,750 for the season, while purchase options ranged from 
approximately $74,000 to $149,000. Discussion focused on the value of maintaining the student and 
community experience, providing safe accommodations for spectators, band members, and student 
sections, and the potential long-term benefits of owning bleachers for use at other district events and 
athletic facilities. 
 
Board members expressed concern about funding such a purchase during a challenging budget cycle 
but also acknowledged the importance of preserving student experiences and supporting community 
events. Members discussed potential collaboration with the City, possible funding sources, integration 
with future athletic facility plans, and the possibility of seeking sponsorships or donations.  
 
Administration noted that city officials have been receptive to temporary bleacher solutions and that 
additional information regarding procurement requirements, costs, and timelines would be gathered.  
 
The Board agreed that further discussion would be needed to determine whether to pursue a rental 
or purchase option in advance of upcoming football games and Homecoming events. 
 
Public Comment 
There were no public comments. 
 
Personnel 
Ms. Garon presented three teachers for confirmation:  
 
• Kelly Raitt – Out of District Coordinator (District) 
• Kathryn David – Kindergarten Teacher (Abbot Downing) 
• Casey Rhoades – OYO, Kindergarten Teacher (Beaver Meadow) 
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to confirm the teacher confirmations as presented (Moved by 
Ms. Higgins, 2nd by Mr. Dubois).

• Lillian Stogner, RMS Head Volleyball Coach 
• Lori Trefethen, RMS Field Hockey A Coach 
 
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to confirm the coach nominations as presented (Moved by Ms. 
Higgins, 2nd by Ms. Hasting). 
 
Votes 
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to create a committee to study ways to increase revenue into the 
district as recommended by the finance committee (Moved by Ms. Walsh, 2nd by Ms. Higgins). 
Following discussion, the Board agreed to establish the committee as an ad hoc committee. 
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to direct the administration to notify the City of Concord and 
offer its right of first refusal on properties under consideration for sale, including Dewey, Eastman, 
and the Broken Ground parcel (Moved by Ms. Walsh, 2nd by Ms. Campbell).  
The Board voted 9-0, via voice vote, to request The Board of Education make a request to the city that 
a representative of the Board and staff be included in any discussions regarding the creation 
of a potential TIF district associated with the redevelopment of the Steeplegate mall and adjoining 
properties (Moved by Ms. Walsh, 2nd by Ms. Higgins). 
 
Other Business 
Superintendent Herbert presented the monthly enrollment report, noting an overall district 
enrollment decline of 35 students since the previous report, with significant shifts among individual 
schools and grade levels. Mr. Herbert highlighted ongoing fluctuations in enrollment due to late 
registrations and changing student residency situations, including increases in students experiencing 
homelessness. Board members expressed concerns regarding class-size disparities among elementary 
schools, particularly classes exceeding 20 students compared to others with significantly smaller 
enrollments. Mr. Herbert explained that late-summer enrollment fluctuations create challenges in 
making staffing decisions. He outlined several potential responses, including staff reassignments, the 
use of instructional support personnel, exploration of Title II funding opportunities, and possible 
budget adjustments later in the fall. 
 The Board requested further review of class-size concerns and possible solutions.

Discussion of acquiring bleachers for Memorial Field resumed. The Board had questions for Mr. Largy 
about total cost and installation fees.  
 
Board members expressed support for waiving the district's bidding requirements due to the limited 
timeline before upcoming football games and Homecoming events. Members emphasized that 
administration should still obtain and review at least three quotes and conduct reference checks 
before making a purchase. 
 
Motion to waive Policy 322 for the purpose of acquiring bleachers due to the short timeframe (Moved 
by Ms. Hastings, 2nd by Ms. Higgins).  
 
Following discussion and direction for administration to obtain additional quotes and report them to 
the Board, the motion passed unanimously, via voice vote. 
 
The Board then considered a proposal to purchase bleachers using funds from the Facilities and 
Renovation Trust Fund. Discussion centered on the long-term value of purchasing rather than renting, 
noting that purchased bleachers could support football games, graduation, track events, and other 
activities, while also potentially being relocated to future district athletic facilities. Members discussed 
authorizing up to $90,000 to provide flexibility for freight, delivery, and potential cost increases.
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – September 1, 2026 
 
Ms. Higgins moved that the School Board authorize an expenditure of up to $90,000 for the 
purchase of bleachers for Memorial Field. 
It is the intent of the Board that, upon completion of the new middle school, the District 
incorporate the purchased bleachers into the new middle school field design, if feasible and 
appropriate. 
  
To provide the Board with maximum flexibility regarding the future use of the bleachers, the 
authorized amount shall be withdrawn from the Facilities and Renovation Trust Fund. If the 
bleachers are ultimately incorporated into the new middle school project and are eligible for 
reimbursement through bond proceeds, the District may reimburse the Facilities and Renovation 
Trust Fund from those bond proceeds. 
  
If the bleachers are not incorporated into the new middle school project, the District may retain 
or sell the bleachers, as determined by the Board. If the bleachers are sold, the proceeds from 
the sale shall be used to reimburse the Facilities and Renovation Trust Fund. (Moved by Ms. 
Higgins, 2nd by Ms. Hastings). 
 
During discussion, several Board members expressed a desire to maintain flexibility regarding the 
future use of the bleachers, including incorporation into future Memorial Field improvements, 
transfer to the new middle school athletic complex, retention by the District, or the possibility of 
future fundraising and sponsorship opportunities. 
 
Ms. Mineau proposed an amendment to remove language by limiting the bleachers to seat up to 300 
spectators, replacing it with broader language to allow greater flexibility in selecting bleachers. The 
amendment was seconded by Ms. Boucher and approved unanimously via voice vote. 
 
Additional discussion focused on language requiring reimbursement of the Facilities and Renovation 
Trust Fund through the general fund if the bleachers were retained by the District. Board members 
expressed concern that such language could unnecessarily restrict future options. 
 
The Board voted via voice vote, to amend the original motion by removing the provision requiring 
reimbursement through the general fund if the District retained the bleachers (Moved by Ms. Walsh, 
2nd by Ms. Campbell). 
 
The Board voted via voice vote, to amend the original motion by removing redundant language 
regarding accommodating spectators (Moved by Ms. Higgins, 2nd by Ms. Sadowski).  
 
By roll call vote, the Board voted 9-0 on the amended main motion authorizing the purchase of 
bleachers for Memorial Field.
